# Import existing roles and memberships

## Roles

The `twenty_role` import identifier is a native role UUID. Labels, workspace/role composites, and invitation or member IDs are not role import identifiers.

Use `terraform import ADDRESS UUID`, or a declarative import block with Terraform 1.5 or later:

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    twenty = {
      source = "glitchedmob/twenty"
    }
  }
}

# Inject credentials through the environment and use a local provider build.
provider "twenty" {
  endpoint = "https://twenty.example.com"
}

# Replace this UUID and match every existing role value before applying.
import {
  to = twenty_role.triage
  id = "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111"
}

resource "twenty_role" "triage" {
  label       = "Support triage"
  description = null
  icon        = null

  can_be_assigned_to_users    = true
  can_be_assigned_to_agents   = false
  can_be_assigned_to_api_keys = false

  can_update_all_settings            = false
  can_access_all_tools               = false
  can_read_all_object_records        = true
  can_update_all_object_records      = false
  can_soft_delete_all_object_records = false
  can_destroy_all_object_records     = false

  permission_flags = ["WORKSPACE_MEMBERS"]
}
```

The example UUID is a placeholder. Read the existing role through Metadata `getRoles` or the [role data source](../data-sources/role.md). Match all existing values in the resource configuration before applying. Import reads server values, but a subsequent apply uses provider defaults for omitted booleans, clears omitted description/icon fields, and replaces the complete explicit flag set.

Import does not bypass role safety guards. The bootstrap account's current roles, workspace default, built-in and non-editable roles remain protected from mutation. Use the data source for those roles instead.

Literal UUIDs do not create Terraform dependencies. Use `twenty_role.triage.id` when referencing a managed role in a membership resource. This gives Terraform a dependency for create and destroy order.

## Memberships

`twenty_workspace_member` uses lowercase `workspaceUUID/email`, for example `77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777/alice@example.com`. The workspace must match the configured provider. There is no workspace selector. Obtain the current workspace UUID from the workspace data source, not a user, member, or invitation UUID.

```shell
# Replace the workspace UUID and mailbox. Use the same authenticated workspace.
terraform import 'twenty_workspace_member.declared["alice@example.com"]' '77777777-7777-4777-8777-777777777777/alice@example.com'
```

Existing pending, expired, and accepted access requires explicit import. Match the current role in configuration before applying. Import records the actual role without changing it, sets `ownership_confirmed = true`, and preserves the same ID across invitation acceptance. A subsequent different `role_id` plans a deliberate change. Built-in/default roles may be assigned if user-assignable; their definitions remain protected.

Malformed IDs, foreign workspaces, operator identity, missing access, and ambiguous duplicates fail import. Expired invitations import as `expired` and plan replacement. Never use invitation links or mail tokens as identifiers.

After an ambiguous send or external native-ID replacement, readable state can have `ownership_confirmed = false`. Inspect actual access and match its role. If the resource already has a state binding, use `terraform state rm ADDRESS` before importing that same compound ID. This changes only local ownership and does not revoke access. See [membership recovery](membership.md).

Credentials and sessions are never import identifiers. Inject provider credentials outside checked-in files. Lost access or a malformed response is not proof of deletion; restore access before retrying import or refresh.
